stem.en: Distilled water plus a spoon of sugar: LED dark. Tap water plus the same spoon of sugar: LED faintly lit. Kabir says tap water "activates" the sugar. What is the better explanation?

text.en: Tap water already contains a few dissolved minerals, which are ions. They carry the small current. The sugar is still doing nothing.

feedback.en: Warmed distilled water with sugar stayed dark. Temperature was tested and failed.

text.en: Sugar needs minerals to become charged.

feedback.en: Tap water alone, no sugar, gives the same faint glow. Adding sugar to it changes nothing.

text.en: Tap water has a bit of salt in it.

feedback.en: Close, but "salt" in the kitchen sense is not the point. Tap water carries several dissolved minerals, and what matters is that they are all ions.

explanation.en: When a fix seems to work, check whether the fix works alone. Tap water conducts faintly on its own. The sugar was a passenger.
